Fact.Name: Meets a Schedule H test for household employees
Fact.Description: #159: general household-employee screener, asked in income sources for every return. Before this, the only household-employee question was asked inside the dependent care sections (cdcc /flowKnockoutHouseholdEmployee). Household employment taxes are imposed by 26 U.S.C. 3101 and 3111 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3111) and 3301 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3301), and 26 U.S.C. 3510 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3510) has them reported on the employer's income tax return. 2026 Instructions for Schedule H (Form 1040), early-release draft (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sh--dft.pdf, SHA-256 685fa1486b3a6e5712c5552da3ef0eb5f7b245dec3d3f28e642e37efe15dbf1e), page 2 (PDF p. 3), "Who Needs To File Schedule H?": "You must file Schedule H if you answer "Yes" to any of the questions on lines A, B, and C of Schedule H." The TY2026 thresholds come from 2026 Schedule H (Form 1040), early-release draft (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sh--dft.pdf, SHA-256 0fbdf600ded379d23f381286a3f9b35d15af062c83072b50de149d5c5afb3077), page 1 (PDF p. 2): line A "Did you pay any one household employee cash wages of $3,000 or more in 2026?"; line B "Did you withhold federal income tax during 2026 for any household employee?"; line C "Did you pay total cash wages of $1,000 or more in any calendar quarter of 2025 or 2026 to all household employees?" The $3,000 is the 26 U.S.C. 3121(x) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3121) domestic employee coverage threshold for 2026, as in the draft instructions, page 2 (PDF p. 3): "you paid cash wages of $3,000 or more in 2026 to any one household employee". The $1,000 is the 26 U.S.C. 3306(a)(3) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/3306) FUTA test, which is not indexed. The screen asks the three line A-C tests as one question. The line A and C exceptions for wages paid to a spouse, a child under 21, a parent, or anyone under 18 are not asked. A yes stops the return; it is never computed as $0. Placeholder false so returns that never see the screen are unaffected.

Fact.Name: Knockout: household employment taxes (Schedule H / Schedule 2 line 17a)
Fact.Description: #159: Schedule H isn't computed. Schedule 2 (Form 1040) 2026 draft (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040s2--dft.pdf), form page 2 (PDF p. 3), line 17a: "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H". A yes to /hasHouseholdEmployeeScheduleH stops the return. That covers a household employee with no dependent care claim, which the dependent care question (cdcc /flowKnockoutHouseholdEmployee) never reaches. Cites: see /hasHouseholdEmployeeScheduleH.
